title: University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN)
summary: University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) is a university in Minneapolis. This entry compiles College Scorecard figures and related sources; UniRepository is not affiliated with UMN.

sections.heading: What UMN is known for
paragraphs: The University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) is a public institution known for its large undergraduate enrollment of 31,855 students. The university maintains an admission rate of 79.75%, reflecting its accessibility to a broad range of applicants. UMN offers diverse academic programs, with business studies comprising 11.24% of the total program share and health-related programs accounting for 5.07%. These figures highlight the university's emphasis on both business and health disciplines within its comprehensive educational offerings.

sections.heading: How to read UMN tuition
paragraphs: The University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) tuition varies based on residency status. In-state students pay $17,214 for tuition, while out-of-state students are charged $38,362. The overall cost of attendance, which includes tuition along with additional expenses such as fees, housing, and supplies, totals $30,061. Understanding these figures helps prospective students and families plan for the financial commitment associated with attending UMN.

sections.heading: Financial aid
paragraphs: The University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) offers financial aid to help offset the cost of attendance. Approximately 17.65% of students receive Pell Grants, which are federal subsidies for low-income students. Among those who complete their programs, the median student debt is $19,500. Prospective students can explore detailed financial information and use net price calculators through UMN's official website and the College Scorecard platform to better understand potential costs and aid options.

sections.heading: Career outcomes
paragraphs: The University of Minnesota-Twin Cities (UMN) demonstrates strong career outcomes for its graduates. Approximately 85.28% of students complete their programs within 150% of the expected time, indicating a high completion rate. Graduates experience a median earning of $57,984 six years after enrollment, which increases to $69,020 ten years after enrollment, reflecting positive long-term financial benefits of a UMN education. Among those who complete their degrees, the median student debt is $19,500, providing insight into the financial investment required. These figures collectively highlight UMN's effectiveness in supporting student success and career readiness.
